assessment.reason: The under's margin depends on Slafkovsky's volume staying near history. Listed absences of Montréal top-six forwards could expand his minutes and power-play role beyond the model's tenth-scaled stress.
assessment.model_case: A projected mean of about 2.3 shots on 18.4 minutes sits just under the 2.5 line, with a median of 2. The weakness is that the projection leans on historical usage. If the forward absences push him to heavier minutes or PP1 shooting duty, the shot mean could approach or exceed the line.
assessment.price_case: Only the 2.5 main line is quoted at even money, with a break-even of a coin flip. The model's fair price is near -148, with a minimum of about -113. The one-book market and the low-weight blend both sit near even, so the large gap needs scrutiny rather than acceptance.
assessment.context_case: The injury table lists Suzuki and Demidov out. It is unclear whether the model's ice-time input reflects their absence, and the resulting role change is the key risk to an under.
blocking_checks: Slafkovsky's line and power-play assignment with Suzuki and Demidov out. Ice time well above 18.4 minutes or a PP1 shooting role would narrow or erase the under's margin.

qualitative_review.countercase: Losing Suzuki and Demidov concentrates offensive opportunity, and Slafkovsky may absorb more minutes and shot attempts. Chicago allowing volume would push him toward three or more shots. Conversely, weaker linemates could suppress his possession time, so the direction is not settled. The market at even money may simply be pricing a higher-usage role.
open_checks: Check line rushes and power-play units for Slafkovsky's deployment
Confirm whether Matheson's day-to-day status affects Montréal's power-play shooters
Reconfirm even money is still offered; the case weakens beyond about -113
